page: Amazon Web Services c7i.large is an entry-level compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by a custom Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at a baseline clock speed of 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Compute allocation consists of 2 vCPUs derived from a single dedicated physical core via hyperthreading. Memory is configured with 4.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, providing a strict 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators such as GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistent disks.

Hardware capabilities feature contemporary instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX-tile, AMX-int8, and VAES encryption. Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2019.0, placing it in the top quartile of evaluated systems. Conversely, aggregate multi-threaded and memory-bound throughput reflect the constraints of its single physical core and low memory ceiling. The multi-core Geekbench score sits at 2518.0, while Passmark CPU and memory metrics register in the bottom quartile. Memory bandwidth tests yield 11.05 GB/sec for uncached reads and 11.76 GB/sec for uncached writes, limiting sustained high-throughput memory transfers.

Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. In service-oriented testing, the instance delivered 3.93 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and 2.35 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Due to its solid single-thread performance paired with minimal overall memory and absence of local disks, c7i.large offers targeted resource efficiency for single-threaded batch processing, lightweight API endpoints, development testing, and front-end microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processor. Its resource configuration provides 2 vCPUs across 1 dedicated physical core, 4.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs, requiring remote EBS volumes. Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core execution with a Geekbench score of 2019.0, counterbalanced by low overall multi-threaded capacity and constrained memory throughput of 11.05 GB/sec uncached reads. Due to the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and limited multi-core throughput, the instance is engineered primarily for lightweight web services, small API gateways, single-threaded task processing, and development workloads that do not demand extensive memory or parallel core counts.
